title: Critical Connections in a Network
prompt:
There are `n` servers numbered `0` to `n - 1` connected by undirected server-to-server `connections` forming a network, where `connections[i] = [ai, bi]` represents a connection between servers `ai` and `bi`. Any server can reach any other server directly or indirectly through the network.

A critical connection is a connection that, if removed, makes some servers unable to reach some other server (i.e. it disconnects the network). Return all critical connections in the network in any order.

examples.explanation: Removing [1,3] disconnects server 3 from the rest, so it's critical. Removing any edge in the 0-1-2 triangle still leaves the network connected via the other two edges of the cycle.
The only connection is critical — removing it splits the network into two disconnected servers.

hints: A critical connection is exactly a 'bridge' in graph theory: an edge that isn't part of any cycle. Edges inside a cycle are never critical, since traffic can reroute around the removed edge.

This calls for Tarjan's bridge-finding algorithm: run a single DFS assigning each node a discovery time and a 'low-link' value (the earliest discovery time reachable from that node's subtree, including via one back edge).
An edge (u, v), where v was discovered from u, is a bridge exactly when low[v] > discovery[u] — meaning v's subtree has no back edge reaching u or anything discovered before u.

solution.approach: Use Tarjan's algorithm to find bridges in a single DFS pass. Assign each node a discovery time as it's first visited, and a low-link value initialized to that discovery time. While exploring node u's neighbors: for an unvisited neighbor v, recurse into it, then update low[u] = min(low[u], low[v]) after returning; if low[v] ends up strictly greater than discovery[u], the edge (u, v) is a bridge, because it means v's entire subtree cannot reach back to u or anything earlier, so removing this edge disconnects it. For an already-visited neighbor that isn't the direct parent (a back edge), update low[u] = min(low[u], discovery[neighbor]) instead, since that back edge offers an alternate route.
